title: Use of a movement and load analysis method called Computer Myography (CMG) in medically and vocationally oriented rehabilitation for patients with musculoskeletal complaints.
summary:
Medically-vocational rehabilitation (MBOR) is a different type of rehabilitation strategy that takes greater account not only of personal needs but also of individual life circumstances. This person-centered approach with active vocational integration offers increased chances of success, not only with regard to participation in community life but also with regard to participation in working life. Successful MBOR therefore requires an intensive examination of existing structures in both working life and specific occupational challenges. Using computer myography (CMG), movement and load analyses of rehabilitation patients can provide valid results regarding load deficits, asymmetries, or functional deficits in the musculoskeletal system during various activities. For this purpose, a series of exercises are recorded at defined times during the rehabilitation program and visualized using an innovative 3D-capable dynamic imaging and analysis tool. This allows for the participatory development of more ergonomic movement patterns in small groups, guided by therapists. Additionally, the results of the movement and load analysis serve as an optimized progress assessment tool for medical staff.
The aim of this study is to increase patient compliance through the involvement of rehabilitation patients in the recovery process, thereby sustainably improving their health-related quality of life. The results are also of great importance for reintegration into the workplace.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Participants in the study can be any individual completing an MBOR (Medical-Vocational Rehabilitation) program B or C at the clinic in Bad Rothenfelde.

Further inclusion criteria are: written informed consent to participate in the study, written consent to data sharing, specific occupational problems due to knee, hip, upper or lower extremity, or spinal problems, good eyesight, and sufficient German language skills.
Exclusion criteria:
Exclusion criteria include: underlying neurological and psychiatric diseases, acute infection, fracture situation that is not stable enough for exercise, and insufficient cardiac resilience.
